description: SUPERSEDED BUGGY RUN: hand-written lexicon with no negation, but the tie-break bias (0.5 per position) outweighed word counts (1/81 per word), so it predicted label 1 for 184/200 examples; 0.595 equals the all-positive baseline.
Lexicon-words-v1 plus negation: a sentiment word directly preceded by not/n't/no/never flips polarity (negated units cancel the plain-word unit and write the opposite sign).

Lexicon-negation-v2 with more negators (nothing/nor/without/neither) directly preceding a sentiment word; negated units cancel the plain-word unit and write the opposite sign. (n_params column reflects a later overwriting run.)
Negation (8 negators) plus ~150 more sentiment words (adverb/comparative/morphological forms and more adjectives/verbs), all whole-word matched.
Ablation of lexicon-expanded-v4 with negation removed (NEGATORS empty): plain whole-word lexicon counts only. (n_params column reflects a later overwriting run.)
Ablation of lexicon-expanded-v4 with LEFT_BOUNDARY off: a word matches as a suffix of a longer token (e.g. 'funny' inside 'unfunny'), no whole-word check on the left.
lexicon-expanded-v4 with the tie-break bias halved (TIE_BIAS 0.5 -> 0.25): a sentence with no net sentiment words is labeled positive only by a smaller margin.
lexicon-expanded-v4 with the tie-break bias doubled (TIE_BIAS 0.5 -> 1.0): a sentence with one net negative word is now labeled positive, so the default leans more positive.
lexicon-expanded-v4 with only a space counted as a word boundary (padding '_' and '=' no longer end a word), so the last word of a sentence is missed.
lexicon-expanded-v4 plus ~70 more negative words (flaws, awkward, clunky, cringe, monotonous, pathetic, forced, etc.), to counter the all-positive bias on negative reviews.
Coverage ablation: negative lexicon only (positive lexicon emptied, FRAC_POS=0), with negation and the expanded negative list.
Coverage ablation: positive lexicon only (negative lexicon emptied, FRAC_NEG=0), with negation (negated positive units flip to negative).
Coverage ablation: negative lexicon at 50% (first half kept, FRAC_NEG=0.5), positive lexicon emptied (FRAC_POS=0).
Coverage ablation: negative lexicon at 25% (first quarter kept, FRAC_NEG=0.25), positive lexicon emptied (FRAC_POS=0).
Coverage grid: positive lexicon at 25% (FRAC_POS=0.25), negative lexicon at 100% (FRAC_NEG=1.0), negation on.
Coverage grid: positive lexicon at 50% (FRAC_POS=0.5), negative lexicon at 100% (FRAC_NEG=1.0), negation on.
Coverage grid: positive lexicon at 75% (FRAC_POS=0.75), negative lexicon at 100% (FRAC_NEG=1.0), negation on.
Robustness check of the LayerNorm-constant trick: full lexicon-expanded-v4 model with KAPPA=10 instead of 100 (a weaker constant offset, so LayerNorm stats vary more by position).
Robustness check of the LayerNorm-constant trick: full lexicon model with KAPPA=1000 (a stronger constant offset; LayerNorm stats are even more position-independent).
Negator ablation: only 'not' and n't flip polarity (NEGATORS=['not', "n't"]); full lexicon, KAPPA=1000.
Negator ablation: only 'not' flips polarity (NEGATORS=['not']); full lexicon, KAPPA=1000.
Tie-break sensitivity: TIE_BIAS 0.5 -> 0.1 (NEGATORS=['not'], full lexicon, KAPPA=1000).
Tie-break sensitivity: TIE_BIAS 0.5 -> 2.0 (NEGATORS=['not'], full lexicon, KAPPA=1000).
Left-boundary ablation under the current config (NEGATORS=['not'], TIE 0.5, KAPPA=1000): words match as suffixes of longer tokens.
Boundary ablation under the current config (NEGATORS=['not'], TIE 0.5, KAPPA=1000): only a space counts as a word boundary.
Current config (TIE 0.5, KAPPA=1000, 3-char boundary, left boundary on, full lexicon) with all 8 negators restored.
Current config plus intensifiers (very/so/too/really/extremely): a sentiment word right after one of these gets a second unit of its polarity (doubled weight).
Intensifier ablation: only 'very' amplifies a sentiment word (INTENSIFIERS=['very']).

Coverage: negative lexicon at 50% (FRAC_NEG=0.5), positive at 100%, with 'very' intensifier.
Coverage: both lexicons at 50% (FRAC_POS=0.5, FRAC_NEG=0.5), with 'very' intensifier.

Coverage: both lexicons at 75% (FRAC_POS=0.75, FRAC_NEG=0.75), with 'very' intensifier.
